valuation_philosophy: Allied Farmers is NOT valued as a mechanical FCF-CAGR DCF on its consolidated historical financials. On 1 December 2025 Allied completed the sale of its 67.8%-owned livestock agency NZ Farmers Livestock (NZFL), which historically generated ~85% of consolidated revenue and is now a discontinued operation. The surviving continuing business is small: 100%-owned NZRLM (external asset manager of NZX-listed farmland REIT NZL, earning management/transaction/performance fees), a Parent Operations segment (governance costs partly offset by rental/interest/dividend income from a $10.5m investment property, loan advances and a ~2.7% NZL shareholding), plus a large freed-up cash/liquid-investment pile from the sale proceeds. Continuing operations posted a PRE-TAX LOSS of $0.517m in H1 FY2026 (dominated by NZFL-sale transaction costs and step-up NZRLM costs) and NPAT of $3.542m for the half is dominated by the $2.110m sale gain and a $2.740m one-off tax benefit -- neither is a run-rate figure. This model is therefore a SUM-OF-PARTS / continuing-operations build: (1) a 5-year explicit DCF of the NZRLM fee stream plus Parent Operations' governance costs and redeployed-capital investment income, capitalized via Gordon growth/multiple cap, PLUS (2) a bridge of net cash and liquid financial assets (cash, ~2.7% NZL stake at market, outstanding loan advances, net NZFL continuing-involvement receivable) added at the balance-sheet date. The self-contained Waikato investment-property SPV (financed 1:1 by the non-recourse MC Redlands term loan, explicitly disclosed by the company as having 'no exposure to Allied Farmers' beyond the SPV) is excluded from both sides of the bridge as it nets to approximately zero equity value and carries no parent recourse. The $172.4m unrecognised tax-loss pool is treated as call-option memo value, not capitalized in the base case, but its likely near-term utilisation is reflected via a low effective cash tax rate in the base/bull cases (consistent with the $2.740m DTA/tax-benefit already recognised in H1 FY2026), with fuller taxation assumed in the bear case where shareholder-continuity or utilisation is less certain. Historical consolidated revenue/EPS/equity CAGRs are reported for disclosure only and are explicitly NOT used to drive the projections, because they are dominated by the divested NZFL business. This 2026-08-09 refresh re-verified every input against the H1 FY2026 (31-Dec-2025) interim report and the FY2025 annual report segment note directly -- the net cash bridge, NZRLM segment revenue/margins, Parent Operations costs, and total-debt reconciliation all tie out exactly to source, and no FY2026 annual report has yet been released (due on/before 29-Aug-2026) to warrant a change in the balance-sheet date. No inputs changed from the 2026-08-08 build; this file supersedes it with confirmatory re-verification.

inputs.net_debt_methodology: Heartland Bank borrowings (0.744 current + 0.979 non-current = 1.723) LESS (cash 10.795 + NZL shareholding at market 4.970 + loan advances 3.000 [0.500 current + 2.500 non-current] + net NZFL continuing-involvement receivable 0.813 [2.182 receivable - 1.369 obligation]) = -17.855 (net cash). The $10.500m MC Redlands term loan and the $10.500m Waikato investment property it finances are EXCLUDED from this bridge -- the loan is non-recourse, secured only against a ring-fenced SPV (Allied FLA Limited) holding the property, and the company explicitly discloses 'no exposure to Allied Farmers' from this structure; including both sides would net to ~zero anyway. RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-09 directly against the H1 FY2026 balance sheet and Note 6 (continuing involvement): cash 10.795, bank borrowings 0.744+0.979=1.723, term loan 10.500, NZL investment 4.970, finance receivables 2.182, loan advance current 0.500 + non-current 2.500, continuing involvement obligation 1.369 -- every line ties exactly to the filing. CSV TotalDebt of 12.223 = 1.723 (Heartland) + 10.500 (MC Redlands), confirming the CSV includes the non-recourse loan and that this bridge correctly excludes it (and its matching asset) rather than double-counting or omitting it.
inputs.fcf_note: Not applicable in the conventional owner-FCF sense -- historical reported FCF is ~85% attributable to the now-divested NZFL business (FY2025 consolidated FCF was $6.764m, almost entirely NZFL). The continuing business's owner FCF is built bottom-up from segment PBT (see projections.base.fcf) rather than adjusted from a historical reported FCF figure.
inputs.sbc_note: Immaterial (~$0.028m FY2025, ~$0.035m H1 FY2026 cumulative reserve), first appeared FY2024. No dilution adjustment applied -- shares outstanding held flat across the projection. Confirmed still immaterial relative to the continuing-ops earnings base; deducted implicitly within the Personnel expenses lines of the NZRLM/Parent Operations segment notes used to build combined_pretax_income, so no separate line-item add-back or deduction is needed -- flagged here per the owner-FCF discipline requirement.
inputs.sbc_source: 10-K equivalent (NZX Annual Report) FY2025 statement of changes in equity / share-based payment reserve
inputs.interest_income_note: Parent-level interest income on loan advances and cash is treated as a continuing revenue line INSIDE the Parent Operations projection (redeployment yield), not stripped out, because it is core to the go-forward earnings model rather than a double-count against a separately-added cash pile -- the cash pile itself is added as net cash in the equity bridge, while the RETURN generated by redeploying that (and new) capital is what is projected in Parent Operations income.

tax_loss_pool_memo.treatment: NOT capitalized as a separate asset in the base case. Treated as option value contingent on maintaining NZ shareholder-continuity thresholds (constitution amended, NZX/RegCo waivers obtained 2024). Its effect is reflected indirectly via a low effective cash tax rate assumption in the base/bull projections (5-9% base, 0-5% bull) rather than a lump-sum NPV add-on, since the pool's utilisation rate depends entirely on the small and uncertain future income of the continuing business -- capitalizing $172.4m x 28% against ~$1-2m/yr of pretax income would imply a multi-decade runway with high continuity risk that is better expressed as a tax-rate discount than a balance-sheet asset.

historical_growth.fcf_note: FY2022 FCF not separately populated in filings; 3yr CAGR uses FY2022 operating cash flow ($3.439m) as a proxy start point against FY2025 FCF ($6.764m).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Historical CAGRs are wildly divergent (equity roughly flat over 5yr, EPS +18%/yr, revenue +9%/yr, FCF +25%/yr) and are NOT applied to the go-forward business. All are consolidated figures dominated (~85% of revenue) by NZ Farmers Livestock (NZFL), which was sold 1 December 2025 and is now a discontinued operation. Projections instead are built bottom-up from the NZRLM and Parent Operations continuing segments disclosed in H1 FY2026 and FY2025/FY2024 segment notes.

wacc_rationale.illiquidity_premium_note: Market cap ~NZ$17.3m at current price; extremely thin trading, concentrated register (WAF Ltd 19.99%, Rem Trustee 12.45%, MD Milsom ~15.8%)
wacc_rationale.concentration_premium_note: NZRLM's fee income depends almost entirely on a single external counterparty (NZL); mandate loss, internalisation or renegotiation risk (NZL's Feb-2026 KPMG capital review is a live example of fee-structure review, and NZL director Christopher Swasbrook's April-2026 board resignation plus an ongoing Propero board review at NZL are governance changes at the client entity worth monitoring, though neither has been linked to any change in the NZRLM mandate to date)
wacc_rationale.transition_execution_premium_note: Business model in transition post-NZFL divestment; continuing operations currently loss-making (H1 FY2026 pre-tax loss $0.517m, and the Parent Operations segment alone ran a larger annualized loss than FY2025's full year once NZFL-sale transaction and finance costs are included); no committed redeployment pipeline disclosed for the freed sale proceeds/cash as of Aug-2026
wacc_rationale.wacc_bull_note: Lower than base once redeployment execution is proven and NZRLM/NZL growth is validated
wacc_rationale.wacc_bear_note: Higher than base once concentration/transition risks have crystallized
wacc_rationale.reverification_note: Re-checked 2026-08-09: continuing operations remain loss-making at the segment level (H1 FY2026 Parent Operations PBT of -$1.146m annualizes to roughly -$2.3m, worse than FY2025's full-year -$1.105m, largely reflecting one-off NZFL-sale transaction costs and MC Redlands finance costs during the transition half), and no committed redeployment pipeline for the ~$8.2m of freed capital has been disclosed. All three WACC premiums (illiquidity, concentration, transition/execution) remain justified and are held unchanged from the 2026-08-08 build; there is no new information supporting a reduction.

base.nzrlm_revenue_base_note: 3-period normalized average of NZRLM segment total income (FY2024 $3.350m, FY2025 $2.734m, H1-2026 annualized $3.086m [$1.543m x 2, total segment income incl. $0.085m other income]) to smooth lumpy NZL-share-settled performance fees. Re-verified against the H1 FY2026 segment note and FY2025 annual report segment note directly -- figures tie out exactly.
base.nzrlm_pbt_margin_check: Actual NZRLM segment PBT margins: FY2024 40.5%, FY2025 48.7%, H1-2026 40.8% (H1-2025 comparative 63.2% was an unusually low-expense period, not representative and not used as an anchor). The 44-46% base-case path sits within this historical range, roughly the historical average -- not aggressive.

bull.narrative: NZL's 'YieldPlusGrowth' framework succeeds -- faster AUM growth drives higher management/performance fees; NZRLM cost discipline improves margins; freed sale-proceeds capital is redeployed quickly into attractive rural lending/investment opportunities; tax-loss pool shelters income for longer as continuity is maintained and utilisation proves straightforward.

bear.narrative: NZL mandate concentration risk materializes -- fee pressure/renegotiation following the Feb-2026 KPMG capital review, or performance fees disappoint on flat/declining NZL NAV; capital redeployment fails to find good opportunities (idle cash, poor yields); Parent Operations governance costs persist and are not offset; continuing operations post small persistent pre-tax losses through the explicit window, consistent with H1 FY2026's -$0.517m; tax losses provide little near-term shelter given depressed income and continuity/utilisation uncertainty.

base.da_capex_wc_note: Light-capex fee-management business; NZRLM D&A (~$0.5m/yr, intangible amortization of the NZL management contract) is treated as approximately offset by ongoing reinvestment/BAU capex needs -- conservative net-zero assumption rather than a positive add-back, given the finite-life intangible eventually fully amortizes

bear.effective_tax_note: No cash tax benefit assumed on losses in the explicit bear window (conservatism)

bear.terminal_bound: n/a -- terminal-year FCF is negative; Gordon/cap formulas are not meaningful on a negative base, so terminal value is floored at zero (the operating business is assumed to be worth nothing incremental, not negative, since shareholders are not on the hook for further capital beyond what is already on balance sheet)
bear.note: Bear-case value is almost entirely the net-cash/liquid-investment balance sheet floor (~$0.62/share on its own), since the continuing operating business is projected to run small persistent losses throughout the explicit window and is given zero terminal value. This is the downside floor, not a scenario where equity value goes to zero -- it reflects Allied's realizable cash, NZL stake and loan advances protecting the downside even if the asset-management strategy does not work.

entry_price.methodology: Base-case interim FCFs (FY2027-31) discounted at the 15% hurdle, plus the base-case Gordon terminal value (computed at WACC, the fair price a buyer pays at exit) discounted back at the 15% hurdle, less net debt (net cash added back), divided by year-5 share count. Full formula: (sum FCF_t/1.15^t + TV_5/1.15^5 - net_debt) / projected_shares[5], t=1..5.

base.note: Entry price sits close to, and marginally above, the base-case intrinsic value ($0.856) because the 15% hurdle is close to the base-case WACC (15.95%) -- consistent with the expected sanity property. Both are far above the current $0.60 price, driven overwhelmingly by the ~$17.9m net-cash/liquid-investment position (~$0.62/share on its own) against a market cap of only ~$17.3m, i.e. the market is currently pricing close to zero value for the going-forward NZRLM fee business and the freed capital's redeployment optionality.

sensitivity.matrix_note: Rows = WACC (13.95% to 17.95%), Columns = terminal growth (1.0% to 3.0%). Base-case FCF path held constant; only WACC and terminal growth vary. Intrinsic value is not highly sensitive to these two inputs within this range (range $0.82-$0.92) because ~57% of enterprise value comes from the discounted operating cash flows/terminal value on a very small FCF base, while the dominant driver of total intrinsic value is the largely WACC-insensitive net-cash/liquid-investment bridge (~$17.9m, ~68% of total equity value in the base case).

key_judgment_calls: Treated the continuing business (NZRLM + Parent Operations) as a small, mature-margin fee/investment operation valued via a 5-year explicit DCF (margins already stable at 41-49% NZRLM PBT margin across 3 recent periods -- no ramp needed, so 5yr horizon is appropriate per methodology), rather than extrapolating any historical consolidated CAGR that is dominated by the divested NZFL business.

Normalized NZRLM segment revenue to a 3-period average ($3.057m) rather than using any single year, because performance fees (10% of NZL's NAV increase, settled in NZL shares) are inherently lumpy year to year.

Excluded the $10.5m MC Redlands term loan and the $10.5m Waikato investment property it finances from the net-debt bridge entirely, since the company explicitly discloses the loan is non-recourse to Allied Farmers beyond the ring-fenced SPV (Allied FLA Limited) -- including both sides would net to ~zero equity value in any case, so exclusion is both correct and immaterial to the result, but is disclosed for transparency.

Added back the ~2.71-2.75% NZL shareholding at fair value ($4.970m), outstanding loan advances ($3.0m: $0.5m South Canterbury dairy loan current portion + $2.5m non-current), and the net NZFL continuing-involvement receivable ($0.813m) as part of net cash/liquid-investment assets in the equity bridge, since these are readily identifiable, market- or contractually-valued financial assets sitting outside the core NZRLM/Parent Operations fee stream.

Did NOT capitalize the $172.4m unrecognised tax-loss pool as a standalone NPV addition; instead reflected its likely near-term utilisation via a low effective cash tax rate (5-9% base case, ramping toward statutory 28% only in the bear case) -- consistent with the $2.740m tax benefit/DTA already recognised in H1 FY2026, but conservative relative to the pool's theoretical multi-decade shelter value, which is instead flagged as memo/option value.

Modeled Parent Operations governance costs as roughly flat in dollar terms (~$1.05m/yr base case) rather than scaling with revenue, since these are largely fixed corporate/board/compliance costs of a listed micro-cap, not a function of the (small) NZRLM revenue base -- despite H1 FY2026's annualized run-rate being notably worse due to one-off NZFL-sale transaction costs and MC Redlands finance costs during the transition half.

Modeled the ~$8.2m of freed capital (NZFL sale proceeds + released continuing-involvement receivables) as redeployed at a blended yield (6% base, 8% bull, 3% bear) ramping in over 1-3 years to reflect execution risk and the absence of a disclosed committed investment pipeline, rather than assuming instant full deployment at a high going-in yield.

Bear-case terminal value floored at zero rather than negative, because the continuing operating business is projected to run small persistent pre-tax losses (consistent with H1 FY2026's -$0.517m) through the explicit window with no visible path to profitability in that scenario -- the downside is expressed through the operating DCF contributing nothing incrementally, not through capitalizing a negative perpetuity, leaving the balance-sheet net-cash floor (~$0.61/share) as the effective floor value.

Stacked three explicit WACC premiums on top of a standard NZ CAPM cost of equity (9.45%): +2.25% illiquidity (micro-cap, ~NZ$17.3m market cap, concentrated register), +2.25% single-client concentration (NZRLM's fee income depends almost entirely on the NZL mandate), +2.0% transition/execution risk (unproven redeployment strategy, currently loss-making continuing operations) -- landing at 15.95% base WACC, within the 14-18% range indicated by the task brief. Re-verified 2026-08-09 that all three premiums remain justified; none lowered given continuing losses and no committed redeployment pipeline.

Reported historical revenue/EPS/equity/FCF CAGRs for disclosure only (they diverge wildly: equity roughly flat over 5yr vs. EPS +18%/yr) and explicitly did not select any of them as a growth-rate driver, since none reflect the go-forward continuing business.

SBC (~$0.028m FY2025, ~$0.035m H1 FY2026) is immaterial and is not separately deducted as a distinct owner-FCF adjustment; it sits embedded within the Personnel expenses line of the segment PBT figures the projections are built from, so it is already captured, and no dilution adjustment is warranted (no evidence of meaningful share issuance from awards).

sanity_check.implied_multiples_basis: Base-case IV $0.856 against FY2025 consolidated actuals (EPS $0.0997, EBITDA $5.988m, net debt $2.905m) for P/E and EV/EBITDA -- these are of LIMITED USEFULNESS here (see caveat below). The more meaningful anchor for a sum-of-parts, post-divestment micro-cap is P/B: continuing-operations shareholders' equity of ~$29.204m (H1 FY2026 balance sheet, the latest post-divestment book value) against the current market cap of ~$17.3m (28.807m shares x $0.60) implies the market is trading Allied at ~0.59x book, while the base-case intrinsic value of $0.856/share against the same ~$29.204m equity (i.e. IV market cap of ~$24.7m) implies ~0.85x book -- both comfortably below 1.0x, i.e. the DCF is not asking the market to pay a premium to the tangible net-asset backing, consistent with a business that is currently loss-making at the operating level.

historical_averages_ex_outliers.note: FY2017-2019 P/B (11.3x, 4.6x, 2.6x) excluded as outliers -- equity was tiny ($1-4.4m) while the company was still recovering from the Hanover/legacy asset workout, so book multiples from those years are not meaningful; they remain in the year-by-year table. P/B stats use FY2020-FY2025. Pre-FY2020 market caps use share counts divided by 10 to pair with Yahoo's back-adjusted prices (10:1 consolidation Dec-2019). IMPORTANT: these historical multiples are all computed on the OLD consolidated (NZFL-inclusive) business and are not a like-for-like comparison to the post-divestment sum-of-parts entity -- retained for context only, not as a pass/fail bound.

sanity_check.diagnosis: No trip -- with an explicit and important caveat. Allied is a transitioning micro-cap where the FY2025 consolidated actuals (EPS, EBITDA) still fully embed the divested NZFL business (~85% of that period's revenue), so implied P/E (8.6x) and EV/EBITDA (4.6x) computed against those actuals are close to meaningless as a check on THIS valuation -- they are not manufactured trips, but they are also not a genuine pass, because the earnings/EBITDA base they are measured against no longer exists. Recording them for completeness (both happen to sit within/near historical ranges, 8.6x vs 7.8x avg P/E and 4.6x vs 4.0x avg EV/EBITDA) is coincidental, not confirmatory. The ONE multiple that is genuinely meaningful post-divestment is P/B: continuing-operations book value is ~$29.2m against a market cap of only ~$17.3m (0.59x book) and against the base-case IV-implied market cap of ~$24.7m (0.85x book) -- both well under 1.0x, which is a sensible, non-alarming anchor for a business that is currently loss-making at the operating level and has not yet proven its capital-redeployment thesis. Base-case upside of 42.7% is under the 100% threshold. The IV is dominated by the ~$17.9m net-cash/liquid-investment bridge (~$0.62/share, ~68% of total base-case equity value) rather than aggressive operating projections.
